name: Nephron
credit: "Nephron", NIAID NIH BioArt Source (https://bioart.niaid.nih.gov/bioart/560), public domain
tags: Nephron This functional tissue unit (FTU) illustration includes cell types related to the nephron FTU in the ASCT+B Table Kidney v1.4 . This illustration was inspired by the Kidney Tissue Atlas Explorer created by the Kidney Precision Medicine Project (KPMP). Multiple histology atlases, especially Human Microscopic Anatomy (Krstić 1991) and Histology: A Text and Atlas (Wojciech Pawlina and Michael H. Ross 2019) were referenced. Cell types and diameters were primarily defined from (Hu, McDonough, and Layton 2021; Layton and Layton 2019). Additional references used (Adam Augustyn 2024). Uberon describes this FTU as follows: "The basic functional unit of the kidney. Its chief function is to regulate the concentration of water and soluble substances like sodium salts by filtering the blood, reabsorbing what is needed and excreting the rest as urine. A nephron eliminates wastes from the body, regulates blood volume and blood pressure, controls levels of electrolytes and metabolites, and regulates blood pH. Its functions are vital to life and are regulated by the endocrine system by hormones such as antidiuretic hormone, aldosterone, and parathyroid hormone." name: Domestic Cat
author: Ryan Kissinger
credit: "Domestic Cat" by Ryan Kissinger, NIAID NIH BioArt Source (https://bioart.niaid.nih.gov/bioart/601), public domain
tags: brown cat meow pet. kitty tabby The domestic cat (Felis catus), also known as the house cat, is a small carnivorous mammal that has been domesticated. It is the only species within the Felidae family that has been domesticated. Through studies in archaeology and genetics, it has been determined that cats were domesticated in the Near East around 7500 BC. Cats are commonly kept as pets or farm animals but also live independently as feral creatures, often avoiding human interaction. Valued by people for their companionship and their ability to control pests, they are skilled at hunting vermin. With retractable claws designed for capturing small prey like mice and rats, they possess a strong, agile body, quick reflexes, and sharp teeth. Cats are known for their excellent night vision and keen sense of smell. While they are social animals, they hunt alone and are most active during dawn and dusk.

name: Trypanosoma cruzi
author: Ryan Kissinger
credit: "Trypanosoma cruzi" by Ryan Kissinger, NIAID NIH BioArt Source (https://bioart.niaid.nih.gov/bioart/634), public domain
tags: cell flagellates Kinetoplastida Parasite Trypanosoma trypanosome unicellular parasitic flagellate protozoa Trypanosoma is a genus of unicellular, parasitic flagellates belonging to the class Kinetoplastida (family Trypanosomatidae), a monophyletic group within the phylum Euglenozoa. The name "Trypanosoma" comes from Ancient Greek— trypano meaning "borer" and soma meaning "body"—a reference to their distinctive corkscrew-like movement. Most species of Trypanosoma are heteroxenous, meaning they require more than one host to complete their life cycle, and are typically transmitted by blood-feeding invertebrate vectors.

tags: bood glass slide smear technique A blood smear—also known as a peripheral blood smear or blood film—is a thin layer of blood spread onto a glass microscope slide and stained to enable microscopic examination of the different blood cells. Blood smears are used in the evaluation of hematological disorders and are routinely performed to detect blood parasites, including those that cause malaria and filariasis.

name: Blood Smear Wright-Giemsa Stain
author: Ryan Kissinger
credit: "Blood Smear Wright-Giemsa Stain" by Ryan Kissinger, NIAID NIH BioArt Source (https://bioart.niaid.nih.gov/bioart/676), public domain
tags: technique A blood smear—also known as a peripheral blood smear or blood film—is a thin layer of blood spread onto a glass microscope slide and stained to enable microscopic examination of the different blood cells. Blood smears are used in the evaluation of hematological disorders and are routinely performed to detect blood parasites, including those that cause malaria and filariasis. Wright’s stain is a hematologic stain used to distinguish different types of blood cells. It traditionally consists of a mixture of eosin (red) and methylene blue dyes. The stain is primarily applied to peripheral blood smears, urine samples, and bone marrow aspirates for examination under a light microscope. In cytogenetics, Wright’s stain is also used to stain chromosomes, aiding in the diagnosis of various syndromes and diseases.

name: Hantavirus
author: Ryan Kissinger
credit: "Hantavirus" by Ryan Kissinger, NIAID NIH BioArt Source (https://bioart.niaid.nih.gov/bioart/682), public domain
tags: Andes Bunyavirales cardiopulmonary syndrome hanta Hantaviridae Orthohantavirus RNA virus zoonotic Orthohantaviruses are a genus of viruses that includes all hantaviruses known to cause disease in humans. These viruses are primarily maintained in rodent populations, with each hantavirus species typically associated with a specific rodent host. In their natural rodent reservoirs, hantaviruses usually establish persistent infections without causing symptoms. In humans, however, hantavirus infection can result in two serious illnesses: hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS) and hantavirus pulmonary syndrome (HPS). HFRS is predominantly associated with Old World hantaviruses found in Africa, Asia, and Europe, whereas HPS is primarily caused by New World hantaviruses circulating in the Americas.

name: Toxoplasma gondii Tachyzoite
author: Ryan Kissinger
credit: "Toxoplasma gondii Tachyzoite" by Ryan Kissinger, NIAID NIH BioArt Source (https://bioart.niaid.nih.gov/bioart/683), public domain
tags: toxoplasmosis Toxoplasma gondii is a globally distributed parasitic protozoan that causes toxoplasmosis. It can infect nearly all warm-blooded animals, including humans, birds, and other mammals. However, members of the cat family (Felidae) are the only known definitive hosts in which the parasite completes its sexual reproductive cycle. As a result, cats play a central role in the transmission and life cycle of T. gondii.

author: Rachel Bajema
credit: "Endocrine Pancreas" by Rachel Bajema, NIAID NIH BioArt Source (https://bioart.niaid.nih.gov/bioart/701), public domain
tags: Endocrine Pancreas This functional tissue unit (FTU) illustration includes cell types related to the islets of Langerhans of endocrine pancreas FTU in the ASCT+B Table Pancreas <> . Cell type and measurements were referenced from (Da Silva Xavier 2018). Uberon describes this FTU as follows: "The part of the pancreas that is part of the endocrine system and is made up of islet cells, which produce insulin, glucagon and somatostatin." Bibliography : Da Silva Xavier, Gabriela. 2018. “The Cells of the Islets of Langerhans.” Journal of Clinical Medicine 7 (3): 54. https://doi.org/10.3390/jcm7030054 .

name: Chorionic Terminal Villus
author: Rachel Bajema
credit: "Chorionic Terminal Villus" by Rachel Bajema, NIAID NIH BioArt Source (https://bioart.niaid.nih.gov/bioart/702), public domain
tags: Chorionic Terminal Villus This functional tissue unit (FTU) illustration includes cell types related to the chorionic terminal villus FTU in the ASCT+B Table Placenta v1.3 . Multiple histology atlases, especially Human Microscopic Anatomy (Krstić 1991) and Histology: A Text and Atlas (Wojciech Pawlina and Michael H. Ross 2019) were referenced. Cell type and metrics were primarily defined from (Hu, McDonough, and Layton 2021; Layton and Layton 2019) and (Rasool et al. 2021). Uberon describes this FTU as follows: "The most distal part of a chorionic villus. A chorionic terminal villus is a grape-like structure characterized by a high degree of capillarization and highly dilated sinusoids. A terminal villus has less stroma and a discontinuous cytotrophoblast layer, and contains 4–6 fetal capillaries per cross section. It exhibits a diameter ranging from 40 to about 80 μm." Bibliography : National Center for Biotechnology Information (NCBI). 2009. “Structure of the Placenta.” In Molecular Biology of Human Placenta, edited by Y. W. Loke and A. M. King. Bethesda, MD: NCBI Bookshelf. https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK53256/ F. M. Burton, N. B. Jauniaux, and J. C. tags: Selenium is a chemical element with the symbol Se and atomic number 34. It is a nonmetal (more rarely considered a metalloid) with properties that are intermediate between the elements above and below in the periodic table, sulfur and tellurium, and also has similarities to arsenic. Selenium – from Ancient Greek σελήνη (selḗnē) "Moon" – was discovered in 1817 by Jöns Jacob Berzelius, who noted the similarity of the new element to the previously discovered tellurium (named for the Earth)

tags: In molecular biology a selenoprotein is any protein that includes a selenocysteine (Sec, U, Se-Cys) amino acid residue. Among functionally characterized selenoproteins are five glutathione peroxidases (GPX) and three thioredoxin reductases, (TrxR/TXNRD) which both contain only one Sec. Selenoprotein P is the most common selenoprotein found in the plasma. It is unusual because in humans it contains 10 Sec residues, which are split into two domains, a longer N-terminal domain that contains 1 Sec, and a shorter C-terminal domain that contains 9 Sec. The longer N-terminal domain is likely an enzymatic domain, and the shorter C-terminal domain is likely a means of safely transporting the very reactive selenium atom throughout the body

tags: Cytokines are a broad and loose category of small proteins (~5–20 kDa) that are important in cell signaling. Cytokines are peptides, and cannot cross the lipid bilayer of cells to enter the cytoplasm. Cytokines have been shown to be involved in autocrine, paracrine and endocrine signaling as immunomodulating agents. Their definite distinction from hormones is still part of ongoing research. Cytokines include chemokines, interferons, interleukins, lymphokines, and tumour necrosis factors, but generally not hormones or growth factors (despite some overlap in the terminology). Cytokines are produced by a broad range of cells, including immune cells like macrophages, B lymphocytes, T lymphocytes and mast cells, as well as endothelial cells, fibroblasts, and various stromal cells; a given cytokine may be produced by more than one type of cell

Other uses include the treatment of maple syrup urine disease and Leigh syndrome

tags: Fatty alcohols (or long-chain alcohols) are usually high-molecular-weight, straight-chain primary alcohols, but can also range from as few as 4–6 carbons to as many as 22–26, derived from natural fats and oils. The precise chain length varies with the source. Some commercially important fatty alcohols are lauryl, stearyl, and oleyl alcohols. They are colourless oily liquids (for smaller carbon numbers) or waxy solids, although impure samples may appear yellow. Fatty alcohols usually have an even number of carbon atoms and a single alcohol group (–OH) attached to the terminal carbon. Some are unsaturated and some are branched. They are widely used in industry. As with fatty acids, they are often referred to generically by the number of carbon atoms in the molecule, such as "a C12 alcohol", that is an alcohol having 12 carbons, for example dodecanol

Advanced generation ALK inhibitors are those which target acquired ALK mutations resistant to the original first generation inhibitor crizotinib, which occur in virtually all AKL-rearranged NSCLC tumours within a year of starting crizotinib therapy. tags: Imatinib is a Type-2 kinase inhibitor. Its main inhibitory activity is against ABL kinase, but it has significant action at secondary targets including platelet-derived growth factor receptor (PDGFR) and stem cell growth factor receptor (KIT). Coronavirus: imatinib is reported to block Spike protein-induced SARS-CoV and MERS-CoV fusion in vitro, potentially by blocking Abl2 at the endosomal membrane and disrupting the actin dynamics that are required for virus-host fusion. It will be informative to determine if this holds true for SARS-CoV-2, and whether re-purposing of imatinib and/or newer Abl kinase inhibitors (dasatinib, bosutinib, ponatinib, nilotinib) could be a viable strategy against COVID-19. This approach would likely to be most effective during the early stage of infection.

name: ROC curve
author: Joseph Rich
credit: "ROC curve" by Joseph Rich, BioCartoon, CC0
tags: machine learning ai roc auc classifier evaluation ROC curve: true-positive rate (y) against false-positive rate (x) as the decision threshold varies, from (0,0) to (1,1), bowed toward the top-left corner (blue base; AUC about 0.8); the dashed diagonal is a random classifier (AUC 0.5). Label: FPR, TPR, AUC.

name: AI agent
author: Joseph Rich
credit: "AI agent" by Joseph Rich, BioCartoon, CC0
tags: machine learning ai agent llm tools agentic AI agent: a language model core (center, blue fill) runs a loop (circular arrow) of reasoning, acting and observing; it calls external tools and reads back their results (two-way arrows): web search (magnifier, top), code execution (terminal, bottom left) and memory or a database (cylinder, bottom right), all gray. Label: model, tools, memory, loop.

name: ReLU activation function
author: Joseph Rich
credit: "ReLU activation function" by Joseph Rich, BioCartoon, CC0
tags: machine learning ai activation relu ReLU activation function, f(x) = max(0, x): zero for negative inputs and the identity for positive ones (blue base line, kink at the origin), drawn on gray x and y axes crossing at the origin. Label: ReLU.

author: Joseph Rich
credit: "AI accelerator chip" by Joseph Rich, BioCartoon, CC0
tags: machine learning ai chip tpu accelerator hardware AI accelerator chip (TPU/NPU style), top view: a square package (gray) with pins on all four sides and a central die (blue fill) holding a grid of compute cores or matrix-multiply units (blue shade). Generic, unbranded. Label: die, cores.

name: Self-attention
author: Joseph Rich
credit: "Self-attention" by Joseph Rich, BioCartoon, CC0
tags: machine learning ai attention Self-attention: a row of tokens in which one query token (blue shade) attends to every token in the sequence; arc width shows the attention weight (softmax of query-key dot products) given to each token (gray), and the output is the weighted sum of their values. Label: query, keys, attention weights.

name: Attention map (causal)
author: Joseph Rich
credit: "Attention map (causal)" by Joseph Rich, BioCartoon, CC0
tags: machine learning ai attention map Attention map with a causal mask: a square matrix of attention weights, queries as rows (gray tokens left) and keys as columns (gray tokens top); darker blue = larger weight (wash, fill, shade, base from low to high). Cells above the diagonal are empty because each token may attend only to itself and earlier tokens, as in a decoder-only language model. Label: query, key, mask.

name: Autoencoder
author: Joseph Rich
credit: "Autoencoder" by Joseph Rich, BioCartoon, CC0
tags: machine learning ai autoencoder Autoencoder: an encoder (5 to 3 nodes) compresses the input into a narrow bottleneck, the latent code (2 nodes, blue shade), and a mirror-image decoder (3 to 5 nodes) reconstructs the input from it; all layers fully connected (gray edges). Label: encoder, latent code, decoder.

name: Chatbot
author: Joseph Rich
credit: "Chatbot" by Joseph Rich, BioCartoon, CC0
tags: machine learning ai chatbot llm chat assistant Chat assistant: a conversation of two speech bubbles, a user message (gray, right) and the model's longer reply (blue fill, left); lines stand for text. Stands for a chatbot or an instruction-tuned language model. Label: prompt, response.

name: Convolutional neural network (CNN)
author: Joseph Rich
credit: "Convolutional neural network (CNN)" by Joseph Rich, BioCartoon, CC0
tags: machine learning ai cnn convolution deep learning image Convolutional neural network: an input image grid (left, blue wash) is scanned by a small kernel (blue shade window), each position giving one value in a stack of feature maps (blue fill slabs); deeper layers have smaller but more numerous maps after pooling (blue shade slabs), which are flattened into fully connected layers ending in the class outputs (right nodes). Label: input, kernel, feature maps, pooling, fully connected.

name: Confusion matrix, multiclass
author: Joseph Rich
credit: "Confusion matrix, multiclass" by Joseph Rich, BioCartoon, CC0
tags: machine learning ai confusion matrix classification evaluation Confusion matrix for three classes: rows are the true class and columns the predicted class (class chips in blue, vermillion and green along the left and top); each cell's blue tone shows how many samples fall in it, darkest on the diagonal of correct predictions. Label: true class, predicted class, correct.

name: Confusion matrix, binary
author: Joseph Rich
credit: "Confusion matrix, binary" by Joseph Rich, BioCartoon, CC0
tags: machine learning ai confusion matrix true positive false positive evaluation Binary confusion matrix: rows are the true class and columns the predicted class (positive chip in blue shade, negative in gray, left and top); the diagonal cells are correct predictions (blue shade with a check: true positives top left, true negatives bottom right) and the off-diagonal cells are errors (vermillion fill with a cross: false negatives top right, false positives bottom left). Label: TP, FN, FP, TN.

name: Contrastive learning (CLIP)
author: Joseph Rich
credit: "Contrastive learning (CLIP)" by Joseph Rich, BioCartoon, CC0
tags: machine learning ai contrastive learning Contrastive image-text learning (CLIP): an image encoder (blue trapezoid, left) and a text encoder (vermillion trapezoid, top) map a batch of paired images and captions to embeddings (blue and vermillion squares); the grid of their pairwise similarities is trained so that matched pairs on the diagonal (blue base) score high and all mismatched pairs (gray) score low. Label: image encoder, text encoder, similarity matrix, positive pairs.

name: Convolution
author: Joseph Rich
credit: "Convolution" by Joseph Rich, BioCartoon, CC0
tags: machine learning ai convolution Convolution operation: a 3x3 kernel of weights (gray grid, bottom) slides over the 5x5 input (blue wash grid); at each position the covered 3x3 window (blue shade) is multiplied elementwise by the kernel and summed into one cell (blue base) of the 3x3 output feature map (right). Label: input, kernel, receptive field, feature map.

name: Cross validation
author: Joseph Rich
credit: "Cross validation" by Joseph Rich, BioCartoon, CC0
tags: machine learning ai cross validation Five-fold cross-validation: the data (each row) is split into five folds; in each of five rounds a different fold is held out for validation (vermillion fill) and the model is trained on the other four (blue fill), and the five validation scores are averaged. Label: fold, training, validation.

name: Decision tree
author: Joseph Rich
credit: "Decision tree" by Joseph Rich, BioCartoon, CC0
tags: machine learning ai decision tree Decision tree: a root split (top rounded square, blue fill) and two internal splits, each a test on one feature, ending in four leaves (circles) colored by predicted class (blue shade or vermillion fill). Depth 2, binary splits. Label: root, split, leaf.

name: Deep neural network
author: Joseph Rich
credit: "Deep neural network" by Joseph Rich, BioCartoon, CC0
tags: machine learning ai dnn deep learning neural network Deep neural network: a fully connected network with many hidden layers, here input (3 nodes, blue fill), four hidden layers of 5 (blue shade) and output (2 nodes, blue fill), every node connected to all nodes of the next layer (gray edges). Label: input, hidden layers, output.

name: Diffusion model
author: Joseph Rich
credit: "Diffusion model" by Joseph Rich, BioCartoon, CC0
tags: machine learning ai diffusion generative denoising image generation Diffusion model: the forward process (dashed gray arrows, right to left) adds Gaussian noise to an image step by step until it is pure noise (left panel); the model learns the reverse process (blue arrows, left to right), denoising a little at each step to generate a clean image (right panel, a cell in blue) from random noise. Label: noise, denoising step, generated sample.

name: Dropout
author: Joseph Rich
credit: "Dropout" by Joseph Rich, BioCartoon, CC0
tags: machine learning ai dropout Dropout: a fully connected network in which a random subset of hidden units (dashed empty circles) is switched off during a training step, together with all their connections; kept units are blue shade, inputs and outputs blue fill. Label: dropped unit.

name: Federated learning
author: Joseph Rich
credit: "Federated learning" by Joseph Rich, BioCartoon, CC0
tags: machine learning ai federated learning Federated learning: client devices (gray laptops, bottom) each train a copy of the model on their own local data, which never leaves the device, and send only model updates (blue arrows) to a server (top, blue shade) that averages them into a global model and sends it back (dashed gray arrows). Label: server, global model, clients, local update.

name: Generative adversarial network (GAN)
author: Joseph Rich
credit: "Generative adversarial network (GAN)" by Joseph Rich, BioCartoon, CC0
tags: machine learning ai gan generative generator discriminator Generative adversarial network: a generator (left trapezoid, blue fill) turns a random noise vector (gray squares) into a fake sample (blue shade square, bottom); a discriminator (vermillion trapezoid) receives fake samples and real samples (gray square, top) and outputs the probability that its input is real (vermillion circle). The two are trained against each other. Label: noise, generator, fake, real, discriminator.

name: Graph neural network (GNN)
author: Joseph Rich
credit: "Graph neural network (GNN)" by Joseph Rich, BioCartoon, CC0
tags: machine learning ai gnn graph message passing Graph neural network (message passing): each neighbor of a target node (blue fill circles) sends a message along its edge (blue base arrows), and the target node (large circle, blue shade) aggregates them to update its own embedding; nodes two hops away (gray) contribute in the next layer. Label: node, edge, message, aggregation.

name: GPU
author: Joseph Rich
credit: "GPU" by Joseph Rich, BioCartoon, CC0
tags: machine learning ai gpu graphics card hardware compute GPU graphics card, side view: a card shroud (gray) with a mounting bracket at the left, two cooling fans (blue fill, curved blades, blue shade hubs) and the edge connector at the bottom (blue shade with contacts). Generic, unbranded; stands for GPU computing or model training. Label: fans, connector.

name: Gradient boosting
author: Joseph Rich
credit: "Gradient boosting" by Joseph Rich, BioCartoon, CC0
tags: machine learning ai gradient boosting Gradient boosting (e.g. XGBoost, LightGBM): shallow decision trees added in sequence (plus signs), each one fit to the residual errors of the sum of the trees before it, so later trees are smaller corrections; split nodes blue fill, leaves colored by class. Label: tree 1, tree 2, tree 3.

name: Gradient descent
author: Joseph Rich
credit: "Gradient descent" by Joseph Rich, BioCartoon, CC0
tags: machine learning ai gradient descent Gradient descent: contour lines of a loss surface over two parameters (nested ellipses, darker blue toward the minimum at the center) and the path of successive parameter updates (vermillion points and line), each step moving against the gradient and zig-zagging across the narrow valley as it converges. Label: loss contours, step, minimum.

name: Hidden Markov model (HMM)
author: Joseph Rich
credit: "Hidden Markov model (HMM)" by Joseph Rich, BioCartoon, CC0
tags: machine learning ai hidden markov model Hidden Markov model: a chain of hidden states (circles, blue fill) linked by transition arrows, each state emitting one observation (squares, gray) below it; the next state depends only on the current one. Label: hidden state, transition, emission, observation.

name: k-means clustering
author: Joseph Rich
credit: "k-means clustering" by Joseph Rich, BioCartoon, CC0
tags: machine learning ai clustering unsupervised centroid k-means clustering (k = 3): points assigned to the nearest of three centroids, each cluster in its own hue (blue, vermillion, green shade), centroids drawn as larger circles with a cross; dashed lines are the boundaries between centroid regions (Voronoi cells). Label: centroid, cluster.

name: k-nearest neighbors (k-NN)
author: Joseph Rich
credit: "k-nearest neighbors (k-NN)" by Joseph Rich, BioCartoon, CC0
tags: machine learning ai knn classifier neighbors k-nearest neighbors (k = 5): a query point (gray diamond) with lines to its five nearest labeled neighbors inside the dashed circle (blue wash); it takes the majority class among them (here blue shade, 3 of 5, over vermillion shade). Label: query, neighbors, k.

name: Knowledge graph
author: Joseph Rich
credit: "Knowledge graph" by Joseph Rich, BioCartoon, CC0
tags: machine learning ai knowledge graph graph ontology triples Knowledge graph: entities (circles) of three types (blue, vermillion and green fill, e.g. gene, drug, disease) linked by directed, typed relations (gray arrows; small gray tags mark the relation type), stored as subject-relation-object triples. Label: entity, relation, triple.

name: Large language model (LLM)
author: Joseph Rich
credit: "Large language model (LLM)" by Joseph Rich, BioCartoon, CC0
tags: machine learning ai llm gpt transformer language model generative ai Large language model (decoder-only transformer): a sequence of input tokens (gray, bottom) passes up through a deep stack of transformer layers (alternating attention, blue shade, and feed-forward, blue fill, blocks) that predicts the sequence shifted by one, ending in the next token (blue shade, top right), which is appended and fed back to generate text autoregressively. Label: tokens, transformer layers, next token.

name: Linear regression
author: Joseph Rich
credit: "Linear regression" by Joseph Rich, BioCartoon, CC0
tags: machine learning ai linear regression Linear regression: data points (gray) with the least-squares line (blue base, 2 px) and each point's residual drawn as a vertical blue line to the fit; ordinary least squares minimizes the sum of these squared vertical residuals. Label: fitted line, residual.

name: Logistic regression
author: Joseph Rich
credit: "Logistic regression" by Joseph Rich, BioCartoon, CC0
tags: machine learning ai logistic regression Logistic regression: binary outcomes plotted at 0 (gray points, class 0) and 1 (blue shade points, class 1) against a predictor, with the fitted S-shaped logistic (sigmoid) curve p = 1/(1+e^-(a+bx)) in blue base; the dashed line marks p = 0.5, the decision threshold. Label: sigmoid, class 0, class 1.

name: LoRA fine-tuning
author: Joseph Rich
credit: "LoRA fine-tuning" by Joseph Rich, BioCartoon, CC0
tags: machine learning ai lora fine-tuning llm low-rank Low-rank adaptation (LoRA): the pretrained weight matrix W (gray square with a lock) is frozen, and fine-tuning learns only a low-rank update: a down-projection A (lower blue trapezoid, d to r) and an up-projection B (upper blue trapezoid, r to d) whose product is added to W's output (h = Wx + BAx). Label: frozen weights, A, B, rank r.

name: LSTM cell
author: Joseph Rich
credit: "LSTM cell" by Joseph Rich, BioCartoon, CC0
tags: machine learning ai lstm rnn sequence gates Long short-term memory (LSTM) cell: the cell state runs straight across the top (blue base arrow), changed only by a multiply (forget) and an add (new memory); below, the previous hidden state and the input (lines entering bottom left) feed three sigmoid gates (blue shade boxes: forget, input, output) and a tanh candidate layer (blue fill box). The output gate multiplies tanh of the cell state (blue fill oval) to give the new hidden state (exits bottom right).

name: Mixture of experts
author: Joseph Rich
credit: "Mixture of experts" by Joseph Rich, BioCartoon, CC0
tags: machine learning ai moe router experts llm Mixture of experts: a router (vermillion) sends each input token (gray, bottom) to a small number of expert feed-forward networks (here the top 2 of 4, blue shade; unused experts gray, dashed links), and their outputs are weighted and summed (circle with plus). Sparse activation lets the model be large while each token uses few parameters. Label: token, router, experts, combined output.

name: Multilayer perceptron (MLP)
author: Joseph Rich
credit: "Multilayer perceptron (MLP)" by Joseph Rich, BioCartoon, CC0
tags: machine learning ai mlp neural network feed-forward Multilayer perceptron: a fully connected feed-forward network with an input layer (3 nodes, blue fill), one hidden layer (5 nodes, blue shade) and an output layer (2 nodes, blue fill); every node connects to every node of the next layer (gray edges). Label: input, hidden, output layer.

name: Perceptron
author: Joseph Rich
credit: "Perceptron" by Joseph Rich, BioCartoon, CC0
tags: machine learning ai perceptron neuron neural network Perceptron (single artificial neuron): three inputs (left circles, blue fill) joined by weighted connections (gray) to one unit (large circle, blue shade) that sums them and applies a step activation (drawn inside), giving one output (right circle). Label: inputs, weights, activation, output.

name: Random forest
author: Joseph Rich
credit: "Random forest" by Joseph Rich, BioCartoon, CC0
tags: machine learning ai random forest Random forest: an ensemble of three decision trees, each grown on a bootstrap sample with random feature subsets (split nodes blue fill, leaves colored by class: blue shade or vermillion fill); their votes are combined into one prediction (bottom circle, majority class blue). Label: tree, vote, prediction.

name: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG)
author: Joseph Rich
credit: "Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG)" by Joseph Rich, BioCartoon, CC0
tags: machine learning ai rag retrieval llm documents Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG): a user query (gray bubble) is embedded and used to retrieve the most similar passages from a vector database (blue cylinder); the retrieved documents (blue sheets) are added to the prompt together with the query, and a language model (stack of blue layers) generates an answer grounded in them (blue speech bubble, right). Label: query, retriever, documents, LLM, answer.

name: Reinforcement learning
author: Joseph Rich
credit: "Reinforcement learning" by Joseph Rich, BioCartoon, CC0
tags: machine learning ai reinforcement learning Reinforcement learning loop: the agent (top, blue fill, a policy network) takes an action (blue base arrow, right) in the environment (bottom, gray, a grid world with the agent as a blue dot and a goal cell in green), which returns the next state (gray arrow) and a reward (vermillion arrow) on the left; the agent learns to maximize cumulative reward. Label: agent, environment, action, state, reward.

name: Residual block (ResNet)
author: Joseph Rich
credit: "Residual block (ResNet)" by Joseph Rich, BioCartoon, CC0
tags: machine learning ai resnet skip connection residual Residual block (ResNet): the input passes through two weight layers (blue fill boxes, e.g. convolution plus normalization and ReLU) while an identity skip connection (blue base arrow, right) carries it around them; the two are added (circle with plus), so the layers learn only the residual F(x) and the block outputs F(x) + x. Label: weight layer, skip connection, addition.

name: Recurrent neural network (RNN)
author: Joseph Rich
credit: "Recurrent neural network (RNN)" by Joseph Rich, BioCartoon, CC0
tags: machine learning ai rnn sequence recurrent Recurrent neural network, rolled view: at each time step the input x_t (bottom circle, gray) enters the recurrent cell (blue shade box), which also receives its own previous hidden state through the feedback loop (blue base arrow, right) and emits an output or hidden state h_t (top circle, blue fill). Label: input, recurrent cell, hidden state, output.

name: Recurrent neural network, unrolled
author: Joseph Rich
credit: "Recurrent neural network, unrolled" by Joseph Rich, BioCartoon, CC0
tags: machine learning ai rnn sequence recurrent Recurrent neural network unrolled through time: the same cell (blue shade boxes, shared weights) applied at four successive time steps, each taking that step's input (bottom circles, gray) and the hidden state passed from the previous step (blue base arrows, left to right), and producing an output (top circles, blue fill). Label: x_t, h_t, y_t, time.

name: ROC curve AUC comparison
author: Joseph Rich
credit: "ROC curve AUC comparison" by Joseph Rich, BioCartoon, CC0
tags: machine learning ai roc auc random perfect classifier ROC reference cases: a perfect classifier (green dashed line up the y axis and along the top, AUC 1), a real classifier (blue base curve, with the area under it shaded blue wash, AUC about 0.8) and a random classifier (gray diagonal, AUC 0.5). Label: perfect, model, random, AUC.

name: ROC curves, multiple models
author: Joseph Rich
credit: "ROC curves, multiple models" by Joseph Rich, BioCartoon, CC0
tags: machine learning ai roc auc model comparison evaluation ROC curves of three classifiers on one plot, true-positive rate (y) against false-positive rate (x): the best model (blue base, AUC about 0.9) bows furthest toward the top-left corner, then a middle model (vermillion base, AUC about 0.78) and the weakest (green base, AUC about 0.64); the dashed diagonal is chance. Label: model names with their AUC.

name: ROC curve with operating point
author: Joseph Rich
credit: "ROC curve with operating point" by Joseph Rich, BioCartoon, CC0
tags: machine learning ai roc threshold sensitivity specificity ROC curve with a chosen operating point: the curve (blue base) traces true-positive rate (y) against false-positive rate (x) over all thresholds, and the marked point (blue shade circle) is the single threshold in use, here FPR 0.2 and TPR about 0.6, with dashed guides to both axes; the dashed diagonal is chance. Label: threshold, sensitivity, 1 - specificity.

name: State space model (Mamba)
author: Joseph Rich
credit: "State space model (Mamba)" by Joseph Rich, BioCartoon, CC0
tags: machine learning ai state space model State space model (S4, Mamba): a sequence (gray tokens, bottom) is read by a linear recurrence in which a hidden state is carried from step to step (blue base arrows) and updated by the input at each step (blue fill boxes, the discretized state matrices), so cost grows linearly with length; outputs leave at the top. Label: input, hidden state, output.

name: Support vector machine (SVM)
author: Joseph Rich
credit: "Support vector machine (SVM)" by Joseph Rich, BioCartoon, CC0
tags: machine learning ai svm classifier margin Support vector machine: two classes (blue shade points lower right, vermillion shade points upper left) separated by the maximum-margin hyperplane (blue base line); dashed lines mark the margin on each side, and the ringed points lying on the margins are the support vectors that define it. Label: hyperplane, margin, support vectors.

name: Tokenization
author: Joseph Rich
credit: "Tokenization" by Joseph Rich, BioCartoon, CC0
tags: machine learning ai tokens tokenizer bpe nlp Tokenization: a string of words (gray rounded bars, top) is split by a subword tokenizer (e.g. byte pair encoding) into a sequence of tokens (bottom), where common words stay whole and rarer words are split into several pieces (alternating blue fill and shade). Label: text, tokens.

name: Train, validation and test split
author: Joseph Rich
credit: "Train, validation and test split" by Joseph Rich, BioCartoon, CC0
tags: machine learning ai train test split Train, validation and test split of a dataset (one bar): about 70% for training (blue fill), 15% for validation and tuning (green fill) and 15% held out for the final test (vermillion fill). Label: train, validation, test.

name: Training curves
author: Joseph Rich
credit: "Training curves" by Joseph Rich, BioCartoon, CC0
tags: machine learning ai training curves Training curves: loss (y) against training epochs (x); the training loss (blue base) keeps falling while the validation loss (vermillion base) falls, reaches a minimum and rises again as the model starts to overfit; the dashed line marks the best epoch, where early stopping would halt. Label: training loss, validation loss, early stopping.

name: Transformer
author: Joseph Rich
credit: "Transformer" by Joseph Rich, BioCartoon, CC0
tags: machine learning ai transformer attention encoder decoder Transformer (encoder-decoder, Vaswani et al. 2017): input tokens (gray, bottom left) enter the encoder (left tower, blue wash, stacked N times as the back outline shows) made of a self-attention sublayer (blue shade) and a feed-forward sublayer (blue fill); the decoder (right tower) has masked self-attention, cross-attention that reads the encoder output (arrow across), and a feed-forward sublayer, and ends in a linear + softmax output layer (gray, top).

name: U-Net
author: Joseph Rich
credit: "U-Net" by Joseph Rich, BioCartoon, CC0
tags: machine learning ai unet segmentation encoder decoder U-Net: a contracting encoder (left bars, blue fill; each bar a stack of feature maps, height = spatial size, width = channels) that halves resolution at each level, a bottleneck at the bottom, and an expanding decoder (right) that upsamples back; gray skip connections copy encoder maps across the U and concatenate them (blue shade bars) with the decoder maps at the same resolution. Label: encoder, bottleneck, decoder, skip connection.

name: Variational autoencoder (VAE)
author: Joseph Rich
credit: "Variational autoencoder (VAE)" by Joseph Rich, BioCartoon, CC0
tags: machine learning ai variational autoencoder Variational autoencoder: an encoder (left trapezoid, blue fill) outputs the mean and variance vectors (two blue shade boxes) of a Gaussian over the latent space; a latent vector z (circle) is sampled from it using noise from a standard normal (gray bell curve, the reparameterization trick) and the decoder (right trapezoid) reconstructs the input. Label: encoder, mu, sigma, z, decoder.

name: Vector database
author: Joseph Rich
credit: "Vector database" by Joseph Rich, BioCartoon, CC0
tags: machine learning ai vector database embeddings similarity search Vector database: a database (blue cylinder) whose records are embedding vectors (rows of small squares, shade = value), indexed for nearest-neighbor similarity search so that the items closest to a query embedding can be retrieved quickly. Label: embeddings, index.

name: Vision transformer (ViT)
author: Joseph Rich
credit: "Vision transformer (ViT)" by Joseph Rich, BioCartoon, CC0
tags: machine learning ai vit transformer image patches Vision transformer (ViT): an image is cut into a grid of patches (left, 3x3), each patch is flattened and embedded as one token in a sequence (bottom row), with a learnable class token (vermillion) at the front, and the sequence is processed by a transformer encoder (blue wash panel with attention, blue shade, and feed-forward, blue fill, blocks). Label: patches, patch tokens, class token, transformer encoder.

name: Word embedding
author: Joseph Rich
credit: "Word embedding" by Joseph Rich, BioCartoon, CC0
tags: machine learning ai embedding word2vec vectors nlp Word embeddings: words as points in a vector space where direction carries meaning; the offset from 'man' to 'woman' (blue points, blue base arrow) is about the same as from 'king' to 'queen' (vermillion points), so the dashed lines form a parallelogram (king - man + woman = queen, word2vec). Label: man, woman, king, queen.

name: k-NN graph
author: Joseph Rich
credit: "k-NN graph" by Joseph Rich, BioCartoon, CC0
tags: knn graph k-nearest neighbors nearest neighbor graph graph network single-cell clustering umap machine learning k-nearest-neighbor graph: each data point (cell, sample or embedding) is joined by an edge to its 3 nearest neighbors, as used for graph clustering and UMAP.

name: k-NN graph with clusters
author: Joseph Rich
credit: "k-NN graph with clusters" by Joseph Rich, BioCartoon, CC0
tags: knn graph leiden louvain community detection graph clustering clusters single-cell network machine learning k-NN graph partitioned into communities (Leiden or Louvain clustering): nodes colored by cluster, dashed edges bridge clusters.

name: k-NN graph neighborhood
author: Joseph Rich
credit: "k-NN graph neighborhood" by Joseph Rich, BioCartoon, CC0
tags: knn k-nearest neighbors neighborhood nearest neighbors knn graph graph network machine learning One node of a k-NN graph highlighted with its k = 3 nearest neighbors inside the dashed radius set by the k-th neighbor; the rest of the graph is gray.

name: RAG indexing
author: Joseph Rich
credit: "RAG indexing" by Joseph Rich, BioCartoon, CC0
tags: rag retrieval-augmented generation chunking embeddings vector database indexing llm ai machine learning Retrieval-augmented generation indexing: a document is split into chunks, each chunk is embedded as a vector, and the vectors are stored in a vector database.

name: RAG retrieval
author: Joseph Rich
credit: "RAG retrieval" by Joseph Rich, BioCartoon, CC0
tags: rag retrieval-augmented generation retrieval top-k similarity search embeddings query llm ai Retrieval-augmented generation retrieval: the query is embedded, scored against stored chunks by similarity, and the top-k most similar chunks are retrieved.

name: Graph RAG
author: Joseph Rich
credit: "Graph RAG" by Joseph Rich, BioCartoon, CC0

Digitigrade: the hind leg's backward joint is the ankle. Foxes leap high and dive headfirst onto prey under snow; forelegs reach down and hind legs trail.

The tail rests on the ground behind as a prop.

At low speed kangaroos walk with the forelimbs and tail planted together while the hind legs swing forward.

Both hind legs move together, the feet trail, the body leans forward, and the tail streams out straight behind as a counterbalance.

Salmon leap falls and weirs on their way to the spawning grounds.

name: Sea Turtle (Crawling)
author: Joseph Rich
credit: "Sea Turtle (Crawling)" by Joseph Rich, BioCartoon, CC0
tags: sea turtle chelonia mydas sea turtle reptile animal wildlife crawling Green sea turtle (Chelonia mydas), hauling itself up a beach to nest. Teardrop carapace with five vertebral scutes and four costal scutes per side, long paddle fore-flippers, short rounded hind flippers, and a head that cannot be drawn into the shell. On land the flippers drag the heavy body forward; the sand is context.

name: Sea Turtle (Swimming)
author: Joseph Rich
credit: "Sea Turtle (Swimming)" by Joseph Rich, BioCartoon, CC0
tags: sea turtle chelonia mydas sea turtle reptile animal wildlife swimming Green sea turtle (Chelonia mydas), swimming, the fore-flippers beating like wings. Teardrop carapace with five vertebral scutes and four costal scutes per side, long paddle fore-flippers, short rounded hind flippers, and a head that cannot be drawn into the shell. Side view: a low streamlined shell; sea turtles fly through the water on the fore-flippers.

name: Seahorse
author: Joseph Rich
credit: "Seahorse" by Joseph Rich, BioCartoon, CC0
tags: seahorse hippocampus kuda fish animal wildlife Seahorse (Hippocampus kuda), upright in the water. Upright bony-ringed body, a horse-like head at a right angle to the trunk with a long tubular snout, a crown (coronet), a single fanlike dorsal fin on the back, a small pectoral fin behind the head, no tail fin, and a prehensile tail that curls forward. The dorsal fin flutters to push it along; the male's belly pouch is where the young develop.

name: Seahorse (Holding)
author: Joseph Rich
credit: "Seahorse (Holding)" by Joseph Rich, BioCartoon, CC0
tags: seahorse hippocampus kuda fish animal wildlife holding Seahorse (Hippocampus kuda), anchored by its tail to a seagrass stem. Upright bony-ringed body, a horse-like head at a right angle to the trunk with a long tubular snout, a crown (coronet), a single fanlike dorsal fin on the back, a small pectoral fin behind the head, no tail fin, and a prehensile tail that curls forward. Seahorses are weak swimmers and spend most of their time holding on.

name: Seahorse (Swimming)
author: Joseph Rich
credit: "Seahorse (Swimming)" by Joseph Rich, BioCartoon, CC0
tags: seahorse hippocampus kuda fish animal wildlife swimming Seahorse (Hippocampus kuda), swimming with the body tilted forward and the tail trailing. Upright bony-ringed body, a horse-like head at a right angle to the trunk with a long tubular snout, a crown (coronet), a single fanlike dorsal fin on the back, a small pectoral fin behind the head, no tail fin, and a prehensile tail that curls forward. Unlike other fish it swims upright or tilted, driven by the rapidly beating dorsal fin.
